Expressed concern about lack of attention in environmental statement to protection of historic, archeological, and paleontological resources. Indicated belief that Section 2(b) of Executive Order 11593, dated 5/13/71, must be observed in contemplating use of ORV on federally-owned lands, and that statement should indicate whether compliance with E.O. 11593 will be assured during implementation of E.O. 11644. Also, indicated belief that statement should indicate whether compliance with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (P.L. 89-665) will be assured during implementation of E.O. 11644;
(e) Geological Survey, Acting Director  advised that they have no comments on subject ORV environmental statement.
(f) Bureau of Indian Affairs, Director, Office of Planning  advised that subject statement had been reviewed and indicated their belief that it adequately covers environmental considerations.
Also, copies of the draft ORV environmental statement under appropriate cover correspondence requesting comments were forwarded to the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Housing and Urban Development. No reply to our request from these Departments was received. In addition to the summarized reviews indicated above, comments were received from the Federal Communications Commission.
All the State Clearinghouses were provided with copies of the draft environmental statement, with requests for comments. In response, comments were received from departmental and executive offices of 33 States and the District of Columbia.
In addition to the advance public notices, meetings, and hearings, the Department held scheduled meetings with State and County government officials in order to obtain their direct input in the development of the environmental statement and regulations.
In summary, a total of 144 responses were received from organizations, agencies, and private citizens, consisting of over 300 pages of comments on the draft environmental statement. All responses have been given consideration in the preparation of the final environmental statement. Copies of responses, together with Interior's comments and analysis on their disposition, are included in the appendix to the final statement. As a result of the comments received, many sections of the statement have been improved in clarity, and the statement is more comprehensive in all respects.
